qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: First-quartile low-cost Pilbara iron ore deposits and integrated automated heavy-haul rail and port terminals provide world-class cost leadership, but Rio Tinto is a pure commodity price-taker on global seaborne iron ore, copper, and aluminum benchmarks without pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (commodity price-taker lacking pricing power, REJECT). Despite world-class low-cost Pilbara iron ore assets and multi-cycle ROIC > 12%, Rio Tinto is an unhedged commodity price-taker. Realized earnings and cash flows fluctuate directly with global Platts iron ore and LME metal spot prices, offering zero pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Pilbara iron ore fines and lump sales are benchmarked to Platts 62% Fe index. Operating earnings swung from $30B+ in 2021 to ~$15B in 2023-2024 as iron ore prices normalized. Because iron ore is a bulk commodity, Rio Tinto cannot set prices above market clearing rates without forfeiting volumes.
